svg.title: Chain of Responsibility
svg.desc: Chain of Responsibility. Pass a request along a chain of handlers until one handles it, so the sender never needs to know which one will. Step 1, The sender decides: ExpenseService picks the approver with if/else: it knows every limit, so a new VP edits it again. Step 2, Link the handlers: Each approver approves within its limit or passes the expense on; the sender knows only the first. Step 3, Pass it on until handled: EUR 300 stops at TeamLead (1 hop), 4,200 at Manager (2 hops) and 18,000 at Director (3 hops). Step 4, Relink, don't edit: One changed next reference links in a VP: EUR 120,000 stops there, and ExpenseService is untouched.

g.text: ExpenseService picks the approver with if/else: it knows every limit, so a new VP edits it again.
Each approver approves within its limit or passes the expense on; the sender knows only the first.
EUR 300 stops at TeamLead (1 hop), 4,200 at Manager (2 hops) and 18,000 at Director (3 hops).
One changed next reference links in a VP: EUR 120,000 stops there, and ExpenseService is untouched.
ExpenseService knows every approver and limit,
so each reorganisation edits the sender again
No default? An expense can fall off the end
Express, ASP.NET Core: act, then call next
Python logging: records propagate to parents
At scale: gateway policies, pipes and filters
